defect_root_cause: The expiration comparison uses > instead of >=, so an entry remains readable at its exact deadline and may be returned stale. Shared dictionary and frequency state are also accessed without synchronization, making concurrent behavior unsafe.

eviction_analysis.eviction_strategy: LFU, with the oldest insertion used to break ties in frequency.
eviction_analysis.eviction_trigger: A write that makes the item count exceed capacity first scans for expired entries, then evicts one lowest-frequency entry if still over capacity.
eviction_analysis.expired_entry_precedence: Entries whose deadline is strictly earlier than the current monotonic time are removed before LFU selection. An entry exactly at its deadline is incorrectly retained as live.

boundary_case_results.case_description: A read occurs exactly at an entry's expiration deadline.
boundary_case_results.expected_behavior: The entry is expired at the deadline and the read returns a miss.
boundary_case_results.actual_behavior: The strict > comparison considers equality valid, increments the frequency, and returns the value.

boundary_case_results.case_description: A write exceeds capacity while an existing entry is strictly past its deadline.
boundary_case_results.expected_behavior: Remove expired entries before choosing a live LFU victim.
boundary_case_results.actual_behavior: The insertion-time scan removes entries with deadlines earlier than now before applying the frequency and insertion-order tie break.

boundary_case_results.case_description: Two threads concurrently read the same entry while writes update the dictionary and frequency counts.
boundary_case_results.expected_behavior: Cache operations should be serialized or otherwise protect shared state from races.
boundary_case_results.actual_behavior: The implementation uses no lock; frequency updates and dictionary mutations can interleave without a defined atomic boundary.

ttl_expiration_analysis.ttl_value_or_source: The constructor configures a default fixed TTL of 30 seconds for each write.
ttl_expiration_analysis.expiration_basis: A per-entry absolute deadline based on time.monotonic() at insertion; reads do not refresh it.
ttl_expiration_analysis.boundary_operator: time.monotonic() > expires_at; equality is treated as still valid, so expiration is delayed past the deadline.

entry_lifecycle_analysis.lifecycle_summary: A write stores a value, a monotonic deadline, a frequency initialized to one, and an insertion sequence. A successful read increments frequency. Expired entries are deleted on reads or during a capacity-triggered scan; remaining over-capacity entries are subject to LFU eviction.
entry_lifecycle_analysis.expiration_cleanup_behavior: Lazy cleanup on a read of the requested key and a full scan only when an insertion exceeds capacity. There is no background cleanup.

distributed_cache_risk_analysis.risk_summary: Monotonic time avoids wall-clock jumps within one process, but monotonic deadlines are process-local and cannot be assumed comparable across nodes. Independent cache instances can also accumulate different hit counts and eviction choices.
distributed_cache_risk_analysis.affected_scenario: A cache entry or its deadline is copied between nodes, or two nodes independently serve the same key while applying local LFU counters and local monotonic clocks.
